findings.evidence: No off-device sink found for any of the three sources. AD2AppInformation.kt:8: the 'Debug' match is BuildConfig.DEBUG, a build flag, not diagnostics; line 18 only builds an unused string from Build.MANUFACTURER and Build.MODEL. ApplicationModule.kt:57: the 'StrictMode' match only registers StrictModeInitializer, whose body is behind if (false) (StrictModeInitializer.kt:13) and would only use penaltyLog. HistoricalProcessExitReasonsInitializer.kt:25-31: reads the last exit record through ActivityManager; the ANR trace is read and discarded (line 30, stackTrace?.length has no effect) and only reason and description go to logger.log (line 31). The logger is not a telemetry path: ApplicationModule.kt:48 provides LoggerImpl, and LoggerImpl.kt:14-23 keeps entries in an in-memory MutableSharedFlow (replay 100) and drops the params map. Its only production consumers of getLogFlow are DrawerFragment.kt:231 (on-screen log list), CameraFragment.kt:100-101 (Log.d to local logcat) and XoViewModel.kt:44-46 (on-screen UI state). No getLogsFlow consumer exists in production code. Build files (*.kts, *.toml, *.gradle) contain no Firebase, Crashlytics, AppMetrica, Sentry, Mixpanel, Amplitude, AppsFlyer, Bugsnag or Datadog dependency. Not inspected: the internals of androidx core-performance-play-services (libs.versions.toml:138), used by DevicePerformanceInitializer.kt:12-13; the app code only reads mediaPerformanceClass and passes it to the same local logger. Step 2 (disclosure search) skipped because is_transferred is false. Case 1.
findings.recommendation: No Data safety declaration is needed for performance diagnostics while the logger stays local, which matches the form's 'no data collected' answer. Any future crash or telemetry SDK, or a remote logger behind Logger, would require updating the form first. Optional hygiene: (1) SystemInfoInitializer.kt:14,20 puts ANDROID_ID into the log panel and, through CameraFragment.kt:101, into logcat; it stays on the device, but a persistent device identifier in logs would become a declarable identifier the moment logs are ever uploaded, so remove it. (2) Remove the dead code found here, per the project rule on unused code: the unused string at AD2AppInformation.kt:18, the if (false) block in StrictModeInitializer.kt:13 and the discarded trace read in HistoricalProcessExitReasonsInitializer.kt:29-30. (3) feature/settings strings.xml:26 (license_text16, 'Consent to Use of Data') says the provider may collect technical data about the device. It is used only by fragment_license.xml, and no code references that layout, so users never see it and it is not a disclosure; delete it, or reword it if the license screen ever returns, because it contradicts the no-collection declaration.

findings.evidence: All three sources are false positives: none refers to the name of the app user. activity_item_full.xml:63: 'full_name' is the view id tv_activity_item_full_name, a text view for a Dota item name (tools:text 'Bracer'); no code references this layout. GetItemInfoUseCase.kt:77: fullName is a game item ability name read from bundled JSON assets (readItem, lines 100-105), with no network call in this file. StreamGQL.kt:97-98: display_name is a field of a response model describing a public Twitch broadcaster. It is received, not sent, and the displayed name comes from stream.userName (ConvertStreamToVOStreamUseCase.kt:22). The app has no user-entered name in these paths. Related check on the multiplayer player name: LocalPlayerStore.kt:15 sets it to Build.MODEL (device model, not a personal name), and it reaches other players through LeaderboardSync.kt:53, so it is not NAME data either. Step 2 (disclosure search) skipped because is_transferred is false. Case 1.
findings.recommendation: No Data safety declaration is needed for NAME. If a user-editable nickname is ever added to the games, re-evaluate it, because the player name is sent to the other players in a room. activity_item_full.xml has no references and can be deleted per the project rule on unused code. The random player id from LocalPlayerStore.kt:14 is outside this data type; the identifier audit should assess it.
